samples.summary: `startCallbackServer` arms a 180s timer that is never cleared on its own rejection paths — the CLI hangs 3 minutes then dies on an unhandled rejection
samples.evidence: `const timeout = setTimeout(...)` (line 351) is armed before `tryListen()`. It is only cleared by the returned `close()`, which the caller can never obtain if the outer promise rejects: `reject(new Error('Failed to start callback server'))` (line 366) and `reject(err)` in the `srv.on('error')` handler (line 385, e.g. EADDRINUSE after 3 attempts, EACCES, etc.). In those paths `login`'s `await startCallbackServer(nonce)` throws before the `try { code = await waitForCallback() } finally { close() }` block is ever entered, so the timer stays armed and keeps the event loop alive. When it fires it calls `callbackReject(...)` on `callbackPromise`, which has no `.catch`/`await` attached in this path — an unhandled promise rejection, which Node ≥15 turns into a process crash. Net effect: `wafflebase login` prints its error, then sits for 180 s and exits with an unhandled-rejection stack. The previous timeout was 30_000 (diff line `-    }, 30_000;`), so this change makes an existing latent leak six times worse.

samples.summary: Duplicated `state` query param makes `isWebOAuthState(stateToken)` throw a TypeError (500) instead of returning 400
samples.evidence: `@Query('state') stateToken: string | undefined` — Express's default query parser turns `?state=a&state=b` into `['a','b']`. The `if (!stateToken)` guard passes (a non-empty array is truthy), then `isWebOAuthState(stateToken)` calls `state.startsWith(WEB_STATE_PREFIX)` (oauth-state.ts:43) on an array → `TypeError: state.startsWith is not a function` → unhandled 500 rather than the intended `BadRequestException`. The parameter is not typed as a DTO so the global `ValidationPipe` does not narrow it. Same shape issue applies to `req.query?.mode`/`port`/`nonce` elsewhere, but those are compared/parsed defensively.

samples.summary: `cells batch` reports any stdin read failure as "Invalid JSON cell data on stdin" and drops the original error's structured `code`
samples.evidence: The `try` at line 123 wraps both the stdin `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` loop and `JSON.parse(raw)`. The single `catch` at line 136 unconditionally re-wraps whatever was thrown in `new Error('Invalid JSON cell data...')`. An I/O failure reading stdin (EAGAIN on a non-blocking tty, EPIPE, etc.) is therefore mislabelled as a JSON parse failure, and because the wrapper is a plain `Error`, `outputError` emits `code: 'ERROR'`, discarding any structured code the original carried.

samples.summary: `cells batch --dry-run` was moved outside the try/catch, so a throw from `getConfig`/`printDryRun` now escapes as an unhandled action rejection
samples.evidence: The diff relocates the `if (opts.dryRun) { printDryRun(getConfig(opts), ...) ; return; }` block from inside the original `try` to lines 147-155, which sit between two try blocks. The stated motivation for the original placement (comment removed by this diff) was precisely that an escape from the action produces a rejected promise rather than the `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope. `getConfig` → `resolveConfig` → `getConfigPath` → `migrateConfigIfNeeded`/`loadSession` do filesystem work; any throw there is now unenveloped. The sibling `cells set`/`cells delete` dry-run branches have the same shape, so this is at least an inconsistency the refactor did not resolve.

samples.summary: Confirmation page's "Continue" href is hard-coded root-relative `/auth/github`, ignoring any mount path
samples.evidence: `const href = `/auth/github?${params.toString()}`;` builds an absolute-from-root path. The CLI navigates the browser to `${server}/auth/github?...` where `server` is whatever the user passed to `--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` / the config profile — nothing constrains it to an origin with no path component. If the backend is reachable at `https://example.com/api`, the CLI opens `https://example.com/api/auth/github?mode=cli...`, the middleware answers, and the Continue link points at `https://example.com/auth/github?...` → 404, and the login can never complete. A relative href (`github?...`) or one derived from `req.originalUrl` would be robust.

samples.summary: `req.query?.mode === 'cli'` / `req.query?.confirm` strict string checks silently degrade a duplicated-param CLI login to a browser login, leaving the CLI to hang the full 180s
samples.evidence: Both the guard (`req.query?.mode === 'cli'`) and the middleware (`req.query?.mode !== 'cli'`, cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:51) compare against a bare string. Express turns a repeated query key into an array, so `?mode=cli&mode=cli` makes the middleware `next()` without confirming and the guard fall into the *browser* branch: session cookies are set and the browser is redirected to `FRONTEND_URL`, no code is ever posted to the loopback port, and the CLI waits out `CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS` (180 s) before failing with a message that names none of this. The failure is silent rather than a 400.

samples.summary: `--raw` is silently ignored when the export format is JSON
samples.evidence: `fmt === 'csv' ? formatCsv(res.data, { neutralizeFormulas: !localOpts.raw }) : formatJson(res.data)` — with `--file-format json` (or a `.json` filename) the `--raw` flag has no effect and no diagnostic is emitted, even though the option help says "CSV only". A user combining `--raw` with a `.json` target gets no signal that the flag did nothing.

samples.summary: Formula neutralization is applied to CSV *header* keys as well as values, silently renaming columns
samples.evidence: `const header = keys.map(csvEscape).join(',')` runs the same `csvEscape` that applies `neutralizeFormula`, so a field name beginning with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is emitted with a leading `'` (the new test `neutralizes a formula in a header key too` pins this). Header keys are structural, not user content: prefixing them changes the column name that a downstream `sheets import` or any header-keyed consumer sees, which is data corruption rather than protection. Escaping alone (quoting) would be sufficient for a header.

finding.summary: `startCallbackServer` arms a 180s timer that is never cleared on its own rejection paths — the CLI hangs 3 minutes then dies on an unhandled rejection
finding.evidence: `const timeout = setTimeout(...)` (line 351) is armed before `tryListen()`. It is only cleared by the returned `close()`, which the caller can never obtain if the outer promise rejects: `reject(new Error('Failed to start callback server'))` (line 366) and `reject(err)` in the `srv.on('error')` handler (line 385, e.g. EADDRINUSE after 3 attempts, EACCES, etc.). When it fires it calls `callbackReject(...)` on `callbackPromise`, which has no `.catch`/`await` attached in this path — an unhandled promise rejection, which Node ≥15 turns into a process crash. Net effect: `wafflebase login` prints its error, then sits for 180 s and exits with an unhandled-rejection stack. The previous timeout was 30_000 (diff line `-    }, 30_000;`), so this change makes an existing latent leak six times worse.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate in every checked detail. login.ts:351-357 arms a non-unref'd 180s timer (CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS = 180_000 at line 188) before tryListen() at line 388. The sole clearTimeout is inside close() (line 373), returned only via resolve() at line 369. Both reject paths — line 366 ('Failed to start callback server') and line 384 (srv.on('error') for EACCES / EADDRINUSE after 3 attempts) — leave the timer armed and leave callbackPromise (line 269) without any handler, because the caller at login.ts:35 throws before reaching the try/finally at lines 57-61 that would call close(). The rejection is caught by runCli (cli.ts:76-91) which calls outputError; outputError (output/formatter.ts:106-112) only sets process.exitCode = 1 and never calls process.exit(), and bin.ts:6 is a bare `void runCli()`. So nothing forces exit: the live timer keeps the event loop alive for the full 180s, then fires callbackReject on a handler-less promise, producing an unhandled rejection that Node >=15 terminates on. No guard elsewhere clears the timer or attaches a catch on these paths; the tests only drive the resolved path where close() is obtainable. In-lane (resource leak, unhandled rejection, broken error-exit flow) and blocking at major.

mergedFrom.summary: Loopback callback rejects any request carrying an `Origin` header, which can refuse the genuine browser redirect and hang login for the full timeout
Blanket `Origin` header rejection can refuse the genuine browser redirect, breaking every login

finding.summary: Callback server rejects any request carrying an `Origin` header, which risks refusing the genuine browser redirect on browsers/proxies that attach one
finding.evidence: `if (req.method !== 'GET' || req.headers.origin !== undefined) { 403 }`. The real callback arrives as a cross-origin 302 redirect from the backend; if any browser, extension, or corporate proxy attaches an `Origin` (e.g. `Origin: null` on cross-origin redirect chains), the legitimate code is refused and, because the 403 branch deliberately never settles the promise (line 227-233), `waitForCallback()` hangs until the 30s timeout and login fails with a timeout error the user cannot diagnose. Only node `fetch` (which never sets Origin unless asked) is exercised in packages/cli/test/login.test.ts.

verdict.reason: The claimed condition `req.headers.origin !== undefined` does not exist in the callback handler. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:283 refuses only on `req.method !== 'GET'` (REFUSAL.notGet); the remaining refusals are missing `code` (line 289, 400) and nonce mismatch (line 296, 403). A repo-wide grep for `origin` under packages/cli finds no header check in any source file — only the doc comment at login.ts:233-238, which records that an earlier revision did refuse on `Origin` and that it was deliberately removed for precisely the reason the finding gives ("a browser, extension, or proxy can legitimately attach ... That would refuse the *genuine* redirect"). The current behavior is affirmatively locked down by a test: packages/cli/test/login.test.ts:102-115 issues the genuine callback with `{ headers: { Origin: 'null' } }` and asserts status 200 and that `waitForCallback()` resolves to the code — so the reviewer's claim that only an Origin-less node fetch is exercised is also incorrect. Two further details show the evidence describes a prior revision, not this tree: the 403 branch is at 283-286/296-304, not "line 227-233", and the timeout is CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS = 180_000 (three minutes, login.ts:188), not 30s. The described hang has no trigger because the triggering condition is not implemented.
